newsitem.title: CHINA: Typhoon Willie kills two, hurts 25 in south China.
newsitem.headline: Typhoon Willie kills two, hurts 25 in south China.

text.p: A typhoon slammed into China's southern island province of Hainan killing at least two people and injuring 25, Xinhua news agency said on Sunday.

Fierce rains and wind from Typhoon Willie damaged more than 18,000 trees, 2,800 tonnes of stored grain, 580 hectares (1,430 acres) of crops and 250 hectares (620 acres) of fishponds in the provincial capital Haikou, Xinhua said.
Officials could not be reached for comment.
About 70 percent of Haikou's streets had been flooded when the storm hit the city on Friday after raging across Xuwen county in neighbouring Guangdong province, the agency said.
Food prices had shot up by several times in local markets and 70 percent of the city's streets had been flooded, it said.
Xinhua quoted local officials as saying the storm was the worst to hit the city in the semi-tropical island in 10 years.
Earlier this month, Typhoon Sally killed at least 133 people when it thrashed southern provinces of Guangdong and Guangxi.
Floods that swept across central and southern China in July killed at least 2,700 people and left hundreds of thousands homeless.
